statements.text: Plasma cfDNA rose with skeletal muscle mass index, a moderate positive correlation of r = 0.43 at p = 0.03.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Plasma cfDNA demonstrated a moderate positive correlation with skeletal muscle mass index (r = 0.43, p = 0.03)
statements.note: The reported correlation is positive and moderate, with exactly these values.

statements.text: Plasma cfDNA fell as skeletal muscle mass index rose in these older adults.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Plasma cfDNA demonstrated a moderate positive correlation with skeletal muscle mass index (r = 0.43, p = 0.03)
statements.note: The direction is reversed: the reported correlation is positive, not negative.

statements.text: The cfDNA measured here came mainly from damaged skeletal muscle cells.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Larger, well-powered longitudinal studies are needed to clarify whether cfDNA, including mitochondrial and nuclear components, can serve as a biomarker of muscle health and sarcopenia risk in older adults.
statements.note: Mitochondrial and nuclear components are raised as a future question; no tissue of origin is assigned.

statements.text: cfDNA values varied widely between individuals, and the sarcopenia and non-sarcopenia groups showed no clear difference.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: cfDNA measures showed substantial inter-individual variability, and no clear between-group differences were observed.
statements.note: Both the variability and the absence of group differences are stated results.

statements.text: FnCas9-AF2 produced significantly fewer off-target effects than high-fidelity CRISPR-Cas9 variants already available.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: FnCas9-AF2 exhibited significantly lower off-target effects compared to existing high-fidelity CRISPR-Cas9 variants.
statements.note: This is the reported comparison against existing high-fidelity variants.

statements.text: Patients whose mutations MUTE-Seq detected lived longer after treatment was planned on those results.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We anticipate that the FnCas9-AF2-based MUTE-Seq could offer a valuable clinical tool to facilitate improved molecular diagnosis, prognosis evaluation, and treatment planning for cancers in various stages.
statements.note: An anticipated role in treatment planning is not a measured survival outcome.

statements.text: Enrichment works by cutting only perfectly matched wild-type DNA, leaving low-frequency mutant alleles available for detection.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: MUTE-Seq leverages FnCas9-AF2 for the enrichment of mutant DNA through the exclusive cleavage of perfectly matched wild-type DNA
statements.note: The enrichment mechanism described is exactly selective cleavage of matched wild-type DNA.

statements.text: Minimal residual disease in the leukemia patients was tracked in plasma cell-free DNA rather than bone marrow.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: MUTE-Seq enabled sensitive monitoring of minimal residual disease (MRD) from the bone marrow of patients with Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML).
statements.note: MRD monitoring was done on bone marrow; cfDNA was used for the solid tumour patients.

statements.text: Cutaneous melanomas in the Chinese cohort carried significantly more of the UV signature SBS7 than those in a comparable American cohort.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The UV-associated signature SBS7 was significantly lower in cutaneous melanomas from the Chinese population compared to a similar American cohort.
statements.note: The direction is reversed: SBS7 was significantly lower, not higher, in the Chinese melanomas.

statements.text: The aristolochic acid signature SBS22 turned up in four soft tissue sarcomas and SBS10 in one gallbladder carcinoma.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The aristolochic acid signature SBS22 was observed in four soft tissue sarcomas and the POLE-associated signature SBS10 was observed in a gallbladder carcinoma.
statements.note: Both counts match the reported observations.

statements.text: In lung adenocarcinoma the PAH signature SBS4 was higher in males than females but unrelated to smoking status.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) signature SBS4 was significantly higher in males compared to females but not associated with smoking status
statements.note: Both the sex difference and the absent smoking association are reported.

statements.text: Patients whose sarcomas carried SBS22 had documented exposure to aristolochic acid-containing herbal remedies.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The aristolochic acid signature SBS22 was observed in four soft tissue sarcomas and the POLE-associated signature SBS10 was observed in a gallbladder carcinoma.
statements.note: The signature is named by its known cause, but no exposure data for these patients are reported.

statements.text: The raised cfDNA in these patients came mainly from necrotic cells inside the liver metastases.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Patients with liver involvement had higher cfDNA levels (p = 0.12) and circulating tumor DNA levels (p = 0.01) than those without liver involvement.
statements.note: An association with liver involvement is reported; nothing is said about which cells release the cfDNA.

statements.text: Brain metastases were found in only one of the twenty-nine enrolled patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: BM was detected in one of twenty-nine included patients.
statements.note: This is the reported detection rate.

statements.text: Among patients with liver involvement, cfDNA levels were significantly higher than in patients without liver involvement.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Patients with liver involvement had higher cfDNA levels (p = 0.12) and circulating tumor DNA levels (p = 0.01) than those without liver involvement.
statements.note: For cfDNA the difference was not significant (p = 0.12); only ctDNA reached significance.

statements.text: Patients still carrying their primary tumor had higher cfDNA levels than patients whose primary tumor had been resected.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Patients with the primary tumor in situ had higher cfDNA levels than those with resected primary tumor (p < 0.01).
statements.note: This comparison and its significance are reported directly.

statements.text: RNA-guided TnpB and IscB nucleases efficiently cut the donor joints formed when transposon-flanking sequences are religated.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The donor joints formed upon religation of transposon-flanking sequences were efficiently targeted for cleavage by RNA-guided TnpB and IscB nucleases
statements.note: This cleavage of donor joints is a stated result.

statements.text: Mobilizing the Geobacillus stearothermophilus insertion sequences required a separate, element-specific TnpA transposase for each element.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: showed that a single TnpA transposase was broadly active for transposon mobilization
statements.note: One TnpA transposase was broadly active across the related elements.

statements.text: Expressing TnpB together with TnpA retained substantially more transposon copies than expressing TnpA alone.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: co-expression of TnpB and TnpA led to substantially greater transposon retention relative to conditions in which TnpA was expressed alone
statements.note: This retention comparison is reported directly.

statements.text: These IS200- and IS605-family elements insert preferentially into AT-rich target sites.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Insertion sequences are compact and pervasive transposable elements found in bacteria, which encode only the genes necessary for their mobilization and maintenance
statements.note: The abstract covers what these elements encode and how they move, never where they insert.

statements.text: Inhibiting ENPP1 raised homologous recombination deficiency scores in the tumor types with the strongest correlation.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We analyzed the relationship between ENPP1 expression and HRD score across the Cancer Genome Atlas pan-cancer and individual tumor types using the Pearson and Spearman correlations.
statements.note: The study is a correlation analysis of existing data; no ENPP1 inhibition experiment is reported.

statements.text: Significant correlations between ENPP1 expression and HRD score appeared in 11 of the tumor types examined.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: significant correlations were observed in 11 tumor types
statements.note: Eleven tumor types with significant correlations are reported.

statements.text: Cluster 3 patients survived better than Cluster 1 and Cluster 2 patients in the pan-cancer analysis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Cluster 3 was associated with better survival than Clusters 1 and 2 in a pan-cancer analysis (P < .0001)
statements.note: This survival ranking is reported with P < .0001.

statements.text: Cluster 1 was defined by metabolic reprogramming, while Cluster 3 was characterized by proliferation programs.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Cluster 1 was characterized by proliferation programs; Cluster 2 by extracellular matrix remodeling, differentiation, and immune response; and Cluster 3, by metabolic reprogramming.
statements.note: The two cluster descriptions are swapped: proliferation belongs to Cluster 1 and metabolism to Cluster 3.

statements.text: Differential methylation flagged 354 genes tied to COPD and 496 tied to GOLD classification, with 125 genes shared.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Differential methylation analysis identified 354 genes associated with COPD, 496 with GOLD classification, and 125 overlapping genes.
statements.note: All three gene counts match the reported analysis.

statements.text: The cfDNA classifier separated COPD from controls but failed to distinguish the GOLD A, B, and D subgroups.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: This cfDNA-based classifier (EPIMETRIC) also distinguished GOLD A, B, and D subgroups.
statements.note: The classifier did distinguish those GOLD subgroups.

statements.text: The methylation signature separated COPD patients from patients with asthma in the same blood samples.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Between 2021 and 2023, 166 participants were enrolled, including patients with COPD (N=80) and healthy controls (N=86) from three hospitals in Andalusia.
statements.note: The cohort held only COPD patients and healthy controls, so no other respiratory disease comparison is reported.

statements.text: The support vector machine trained on cfDNA methylation separated COPD and control groups completely, allowing a hard-margin model.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The SVM classifier trained on cfDNA methylation features achieved complete separation between COPD and control groups, enabling a hard-margin model.
statements.note: Complete separation and the hard-margin model are stated results.

statements.text: VarNet-T needs a matched normal sample alongside the tumor reads to call somatic variants accurately.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: an end-to-end weakly supervised deep learning framework for accurately identifying somatic variants from aligned tumor reads without a matched normal sample
statements.note: The method is built precisely to work without a matched normal sample.

statements.text: Benchmarking on public datasets placed VarNet-T 20-33% ahead of existing somatic variant callers.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: demonstrating 20-33% performance improvement over existing methods
statements.note: This is the reported improvement range.

statements.text: VarNet-T called variants faster and with less compute than conventional matched-normal callers.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Overall, the improved accuracy of VarNet-T has the potential to enhance the utility of tumor-only sequencing in cancer research and clinical molecular diagnostics.
statements.note: Only accuracy is benchmarked; runtime and computational cost are never reported.

statements.text: For classifying TMB-high status, VarNet-T was more than three times as accurate as existing methods.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: VarNet-T demonstrates >3x higher accuracy in TMB-high status classification
statements.note: The >3x accuracy gain for TMB-high classification is stated.

statements.text: Three hundred ten researchers gathered in Saint-Malo, France, from 20 to 23 April 2024 for the fourth ICTE.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: From April 20 to 23, 2024, three hundred ten researchers from around the world gathered in Saint-Malo, France, at the fourth International Congress on Transposable Elements (ICTE 2024)
statements.note: The attendance, dates, place and edition all match.

statements.text: Most talks at this edition dealt with plant transposable elements.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This fourth edition offered two keynote presentations and four sessions presenting the latest findings and encouraging discussions on the following topics: (1) TEs, genome evolution and adaptation; (2) TEs in health and diseases; (3) TE control and epigenetics; (4) Transposition mechanisms and applications.
statements.note: The programme is listed by theme, with nothing about which organisms the talks covered.

statements.text: The congress has been held every two years since 2008.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: ICTE has been held every four years since 2008
statements.note: The interval is four years, not two.

statements.text: Just over three quarters of participants, 77%, were attending an ICTE meeting for the first time.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with 77% of the participants attending ICTE for the first time
statements.note: 77% first-time attendance is the reported figure.

statements.text: Twenty high-quality genomes showed that Regiella evolution is driven largely by gene gains carried by mobile genetic elements.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: By generating 20 high-quality genomes, we found that Regiella 's evolution is driven largely by gene gains mediated by mobile genetic elements (MGEs).
statements.note: Both the genome count and the gene-gain conclusion are stated.

statements.text: Protection against the fungal pathogen Pandora neoaphidis was conferred by strains with and without pRILSR1 alike.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: only pRILSR1-bearing strains confer protection against the fungal pathogen Pandora neoaphidis
statements.note: Protection was restricted to strains carrying pRILSR1.

statements.text: A protective strain that lost the plasmid in culture also lost protection, showing pRILSR1 is required for defence.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: loss of the plasmid by a protective strain in culture resulted in the loss of protection, indicating that pRILSR1 is required for the defensive phenotype
statements.note: The plasmid-loss experiment and its interpretation are reported.

statements.text: Carrying pRILSR1 imposes a growth cost on Regiella when no fungal pathogen is present.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In a multiyear field study, pRILSR1 frequency varied systematically among host plant-associated pea aphid populations and predicted differences in symbiont-mediated fungal resistance.
statements.note: Plasmid frequencies across populations are reported, but no fitness cost of carriage is measured.

statements.text: Chlorite residues were measured in the salad samples from which the integron hosts were isolated.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Chlorine-derived compounds such as acidified sodium chlorite and chloride dioxide are used to disinfectant raw vegetables in food processing facilities, suggesting selection for chlorite resistance in phylloplane integrons.
statements.note: Disinfectant use is context and residue monitoring is recommended; no residue measurements are reported.

statements.text: The pre-clinical class 1 integrons sequenced from Pseudomonas and Erwinia hosts lay outside any transposon.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We whole-genome sequenced Pseudomonas and Erwinia hosts of pre-clinical class 1 integrons that are embedded in Tn402-like transposons.
statements.note: Those integrons were embedded in Tn402-like transposons.

statements.text: Class 1 integrons in ready-to-eat salads sat in Bacteroidota and Pseudomonadota hosts, including four genera not previously linked to intI1.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Ready-to-eat salads carried class 1 integrons from the phyla Bacteroidota and Pseudomonadota, including four novel genera that were previously not known to be associated with intI1.
statements.note: The phyla and the four novel genera are reported findings.

statements.text: The proximal gene cassette in these integrons encoded chlorite dismutase and experimentally conferred chlorite resistance.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The proximal gene cassette in these integrons was identified as a chlorite dismutase gene cassette, which we showed experimentally to confer chlorite resistance.
statements.note: The cassette identity and its experimentally shown resistance are both stated.

statements.text: In 430 patients with matched tumor and blood, median concordance was 97% for coding and 88% for clinical oncogenic mutations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: matched tumor and blood specimens (n = 430 patients) revealed high concordance for coding (median = 97%) and clinical oncogenic mutations (median = 88% concordance)
statements.note: Both median concordance figures and the sample size match.

statements.text: Serial cfDNA sampling during treatment detected relapse earlier than imaging in this cohort.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: indicating a diagnostic role for cfDNA from blood extending beyond the identification of companion therapeutics to patient screening and monitoring
statements.note: A monitoring role is proposed, but no serial sampling or comparison with imaging is reported.

statements.text: Actionable mutations appeared only in cfDNA for 48 patients (11%), and only in tumor tissue for 23 patients (5%).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: An additional 48 patients (11%) had actionable mutations detected only in cfDNA assays, whereas 23 patients (5%) had mutations in tumor only.
statements.note: Both discordant groups and their percentages are reported.

statements.text: cfDNA levels in diagnostic blood specimens showed no relation to survival duration once age, sex, tumor type and stage were accounted for.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Cell-free DNA levels from diagnostic blood specimens were a strong indicator of patient survival duration independent of age, sex, tumor type, and stage
statements.note: cfDNA was a strong survival indicator independent of exactly those factors.

statements.text: Peripheral ctDNA rose after neoadjuvant chemotherapy compared with the level before stent placement.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: After neoadjuvant chemotherapy, peripheral ctDNA decreased compared to before stent placement.
statements.note: ctDNA decreased rather than increased after chemotherapy.

statements.text: Every stent placement succeeded, with no perforation, displacement, re-obstruction, or perioperative deaths.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The stent placement success rate was 100%, with no cases of perforation, displacement, or re-obstruction, and no perioperative deaths.
statements.note: A 100% success rate with none of those complications is reported.

statements.text: Changes in cfDNA and ctDNA across the four sampling time points were not statistically significant.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: There were no statistically significant differences in cfDNA and ctDNA changes at the four time points during the treatment process.
statements.note: The absence of significant change across the four time points is the stated result.

statements.text: Patients whose ctDNA stayed low through treatment had fewer recurrences during follow-up.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study did not find an increase in ctDNA after stent placement combined with chemotherapy, suggesting that the model of stent placement combined with neoadjuvant chemotherapy for obstructive colon cancer may be a safe and reliable therapy.
statements.note: Safety is inferred from ctDNA dynamics alone; no recurrence or survival follow-up is reported.

statements.text: High GRWD1 expression went with poor prognosis in lower grade glioma, cutaneous melanoma and clear cell renal carcinoma carrying wild-type p53.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: high expression of GRWD1 is associated with a poor prognosis for lower grade glioma (LGG) of the brain, skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM), and kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC) carrying wild-type p53
statements.note: Exactly these three wild-type p53 tumor types are reported.

statements.text: Knocking down GRWD1 restored p53 levels and slowed growth in glioma cell lines.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Here, we mined the TCGA (The Cancer Genome Atlas) database to gain in-depth insight into the clinical relevance of GRWD1.
statements.note: This work is a database analysis; no knockdown experiment is reported.

statements.text: In patients whose GRWD1 gene was diploid, high GRWD1 expression carried no prognostic association.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: even in patients with a diploid GRWD1 gene, high GRWD1 expression was associated with a poor prognosis for LGG, SKCM, and KIRC carrying wild-type p53
statements.note: The association with poor prognosis held in diploid-gene patients too.

statements.text: Copy number alterations at the GRWD1 gene are one determinant of how much GRWD1 a tumor expresses.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: copy number alterations in the GRWD1 gene are one determinant of GRWD1 expression level
statements.note: This determinant of expression level is stated directly.

statements.text: SBS88-positive tumors made up 7.5% of the 5,292 colorectal cancers, and 98.7% of them were MSS or MSI-low.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In total, 7.5% (398/5,292) of the CRCs were SBS88-positive, of which 98.7% (392/398) were microsatellite stable/microsatellite instability low (MSS/MSI-L)
statements.note: Both proportions match the reported counts.

statements.text: SBS88-positive colorectal cancers had worse cancer-specific survival than SBS88-negative cancers after stratification by age, sex, study and stage.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: SBS88-positive CRCs were associated with better CRC-specific survival (p=0.007; hazard ratio of 0.69, 95% CI=0.52-0.90) when stratified by age, sex, study, and by stage.
statements.note: Survival was better, with a hazard ratio below one.

statements.text: Among MSS/MSI-L tumors, SBS88 positivity was commoner in the distal colon and rectum than in the proximal colon.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: SBS88 positive CRCs were associated with the distal colon (OR=1.84, 95% CI=1.40-2.42, p=1×10 -5 ) and rectum (OR=1.90, 95% CI=1.44-2.51, p=6×10 -6 ) tumor sites compared with the proximal colon
statements.note: Both site odds ratios exceed one relative to the proximal colon.

statements.text: Patients with SBS88-positive tumors carried pks-positive Escherichia coli in their stool more often than patients with SBS88-negative tumors.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The mutational signature SBS88 mechanistically links CRC development with the strain of Escherichia coli harboring the pks island that produces the genotoxin colibactin, but the genomic, pathological and survival characteristics associated with SBS88-positive tumors are unknown.
statements.note: The bacterial origin of the signature is background; no stool or microbiome testing is reported.

statements.text: Deleting a MIR element from a contact anchor weakened that chromatin contact.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: it cannot distinguish whether transposable elements actively drive chromatin contacts or are passive markers of chromatin states
statements.note: The analysis is observational and settles no causality; no deletion experiment is reported.

statements.text: Ancient families MIR and L2 preferentially form homotypic pairs at chromatin contacts, while young Alu and SVA families avoid such pairing.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Ancient mammalian transposable element families (MIR, L2) preferentially form homotypic pairs at chromatin contacts, while young primate-specific families (Alu, SVA) actively avoid homotypic pairing.
statements.note: This contrast between ancient and young families is the stated result.

statements.text: MIR and L2, unrelated in sequence, differed sharply in pairing behaviour, pointing to a mechanism that depends on sequence similarity.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Unexpectedly, sequence-unrelated families like MIR and L2 showed similarly strong pairing behavior, indicating a mechanism independent of DNA sequence similarity.
statements.note: Their pairing behaviour was similar, which argued for sequence-independence.

statements.text: Depletion of homotypic pairs in contact-poor regions was larger than their enrichment at focal contacts.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The depletion of homotypic pairs in contact-poor regions exceeded their enrichment at focal contacts
statements.note: The reported magnitude comparison runs in exactly this direction.

statements.text: Plasma cell-free DNA was obtained from 19 healthy blood donors and 22 uveal melanoma patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Plasma cfDNA was isolated from healthy blood donors (HBDs, N = 19) and UM patients (N = 22).
statements.note: Both group sizes match the stated sampling.

statements.text: Methylation profiles clustered melanoma apart from healthy donors and separated high-risk from intermediate-risk patients, with outliers in the latter comparison.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Distinct clustering was observed between UM and HBDs samples, and between HR and IR samples, although outliers were present in the latter comparison.
statements.note: Both separations and the outliers are reported.

statements.text: The methylation signature identified which BAP1-mutated patients developed metastases within two years.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: However, its role in monitoring disease progression requires further validation.
statements.note: The pilot reports group separation only; no follow-up test of metastasis timing is reported.

statements.text: Gene set enrichment implicated eight canonical pathways, none of them a kinase signalling cascade.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: GSEA implicated eight canonical pathways including the S100 Family Signaling Pathway and RAF/MAP kinase cascade, which are linked to tumorigenesis and immune processes.
statements.note: One of the eight pathways named is the RAF/MAP kinase cascade.

statements.text: By digital PCR, higher urinary cfDNA went with lower odds of rejection.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: higher TTV was associated with lower rejection odds, whereas higher cfDNA was associated with greater rejection odds
statements.note: Higher cfDNA carried greater, not lower, rejection odds; the inverse association belongs to TTV.

statements.text: Across 544 urine samples the TTV/cfDNA ratio was significantly lower in rejection than in non-rejection samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Among 544 unique urine samples, the urinary TTV/cfDNA ratio was significantly lower in rejection than in non-rejection samples (P<0.0001).
statements.note: The sample count and the direction with P<0.0001 are reported.

statements.text: A nominal logistic model built on digital PCR measurements reached an AUROC of 0.76 for rejection.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A nominal logistic model incorporating dPCR measurements achieved an AUROC of 0.76
statements.note: That AUROC is reported for the dPCR-based model.

statements.text: Blood donor-derived cfDNA measured in the same recipients performed worse than the urinary ratio.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Urine samples from 334 kidney transplant recipients were analyzed in association with kidney biopsies performed within 30 days of sample collection.
statements.note: Only urine was assayed against biopsy results; no blood-based comparator is reported.

statements.text: Over 2,000 micro-RNAs were detected, 56 of them differentially expressed, and four were confirmed in an independent batch.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We detected over 2000 different micro-RNAs of which 56 were differentially expressed. Dysregulation of four micro-RNAs was confirmed in an independent batch of cell-free RNA.
statements.note: All three counts match the reported results.

statements.text: The mutant neurons released less dopamine than their gene-corrected isogenic controls.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We successfully isolated extracellular vesicles from induced pluripotent stem cell-derived human dopaminergic neurons.
statements.note: The neurons are dopaminergic, but no functional measurement such as dopamine release is reported.

statements.text: LRRK2 expression and kinase activity correlated closely with the micro-RNA expression levels measured.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Finally, we showed poor correlation between LRRK2 expression or activity and miRNA expression levels.
statements.note: The correlation with LRRK2 expression and activity was poor.

statements.text: Changes in the cell-free micro-RNAome tracked closely with changes in the cellular micro-RNAome.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We discovered a high correlation between changes in the cell-free and cellular micro-RNAomes.
statements.note: A high correlation between the two compartments is reported.

statements.text: More than 5.2 million short inverted repeats were catalogued in the human genome and examined across six common cancer types.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we systematically identified over 5.2 million SIRs in the human genome and analyzed their mutational patterns across six common cancer types
statements.note: Both the repeat count and the number of cancer types match.

statements.text: Raised INDEL density in SIR spacer regions was cancer-type specific, while SNV and breakpoint density rose consistently across cancers.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We found that increased small insertion and deletion (INDEL) density within SIR spacer regions represents a consistent feature across cancers, whereas elevated single nucleotide variant (SNV) and structural breakpoint density is cancer-type specific.
statements.note: The two patterns are swapped: INDEL density was the consistent feature.

statements.text: Osteosarcoma patients whose tumors carried more SIR-associated mutations had shorter overall survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our findings highlight SIRs as mutational hotspots and potential drivers of osteosarcoma pathogenesis.
statements.note: The work maps mutation density; no patient outcome analysis is reported.

statements.text: Whole-genome sequencing of 13 osteosarcoma patients showed both SNVs and INDELs significantly enriched in SIR spacer regions.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Integrating whole-genome sequencing data from 13 OS patients, we found that both SNVs and INDELs are significantly enriched within SIR spacer regions in OS.
statements.note: The patient count and the enrichment of both variant classes are reported.

statements.text: Median donor-derived cfDNA was 0.37% in DSA-negative samples against 3.15% in DSA-positive samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The median percentage of dd-cfDNA in plasma samples with concomitant DSA negative results was significantly less than in DSA positive samples (0.37% vs. 3.15%, p = 0.002).
statements.note: Both medians and the significant difference are reported.

statements.text: Applying the 0.7% threshold prospectively cut the number of biopsies performed in this UK centre.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: AlloSeq cfDNA (CareDx) with the optimal threshold showed an acceptable level of discrimination of biopsy-proven rejection and a potential to reduce the number of biopsies performed.
statements.note: A potential reduction is inferred from retrospective threshold analysis; no prospective implementation is reported.

statements.text: Samples with elevated creatinine had significantly higher median donor-derived cfDNA than samples without.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: There was no significant difference in the median percentage of dd-cfDNA in plasma samples with concomitant samples with elevated creatinine levels (0.41% vs. 0.36%, p = 0.779).
statements.note: That comparison was not significant (p = 0.779).

statements.text: dd-cfDNA separated biopsy-defined rejection from no rejection with an AUC of 0.737, and the best threshold was 0.7%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: dd-cfDNA levels distinguished biopsy-defined rejection from no rejection with an acceptable AUC of 0.737 (95% CI, 0.485-0.987). The %dd-cfDNA threshold maximising overall correct classification was 0.7%.
statements.note: Both the AUC and the optimal threshold are reported.

statements.text: Median overall survival was shorter in SVM-low patients than in SVM-high patients, 6.40 against 17.30 months.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: median overall survival (mOS) (17.30 vs. 6.40 months; HR =0.159; P=0.002) than SVM-high patients
statements.note: SVM-low patients had the longer survival, 17.30 versus 6.40 months.

statements.text: The model's area under the curve was 0.87 in OAK, 0.92 in POPLAR and 0.83 in the local cohort.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: area under the ROC curve (AUC) =0.87 in OAK, 0.92 in POPLAR, and 0.83 in the local cohort
statements.note: All three AUC values match.

statements.text: SVM-low patients had a median progression-free survival of 12.80 months against 3.00 months for SVM-high patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: had significantly longer median progression-free survival (mPFS) [12.80 vs. 3.00 months; hazard ratio (HR) =0.191; P=0.002]
statements.note: These median PFS values and their direction are reported.

statements.text: Patients carrying the 41-gene signature benefited from adding anti-VEGF therapy to their immunotherapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Functional enrichment of the 41-gene signature highlighted VEGF, JAK-STAT, and Ras signalling pathways in ICI resistance.
statements.note: Pathway enrichment points to resistance biology; no combination-treatment outcome is reported.

statements.text: Of roughly 4,300 annotated human-specific transposons, 289 were reproducibly accessible in the aggregates.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Of ∼4,300 annotated human-specific transposons, 289 were reproducibly accessible in the aggregates.
statements.note: Both the catalogue size and the accessible count match.

statements.text: Accessible elements lay closer to genes, in gene-dense neighbourhoods, with more highly expressed neighbouring transcripts than inaccessible ones.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Relative to inaccessible elements, these were closer to genes, occupied gene-dense neighborhoods, and had more highly expressed neighboring transcripts.
statements.note: All three contrasts with inaccessible elements are reported.

statements.text: Removing TRIM28 from the aggregates opened further human-specific transposons.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: protein interaction analysis of the genes near accessible elements recovered a module built around TRIM28 and multiple KRAB zinc-finger proteins
statements.note: The TRIM28 module comes from protein interaction analysis; no knockout experiment is reported.

statements.text: Accessibility was spread evenly across the human-specific families, with no family over-represented.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Co-option was strongly family-biased in both extent and content, with SVA-F and LTR5Hs over-represented among accessible elements
statements.note: Co-option was strongly family-biased, with SVA-F and LTR5Hs over-represented.

statements.text: Patients with a large B3 fraction responded poorly to chemotherapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings suggest that fatty acid metabolic reprogramming and CD44-LGALS9-mediated immune evasion play roles in tumor maintenance within the cardiac environment, offering a preliminary basis for future targeted therapeutic intervention.
statements.note: Therapy appears only as a future direction; no treatment response data are reported.

statements.text: Single-cell analysis of these cardiac lymphomas resolved five distinct malignant B-cell states, one of them the B3 subset.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Single-cell analysis identified five distinct malignant B-cell states, including a B3 subset defined by subclonal diversification and enriched fatty acid metabolism-MAPK signaling.
statements.note: Five malignant states including B3 are reported.

statements.text: Chromosomal instability was ruled out as a contributor to disease progression in these tumors.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Our data implicate chromosomal instability (CIN) as a potential driver of disease progression, likely by modulating cellular sensitivity to metabolic stress.
statements.note: Chromosomal instability is implicated as a driver, not excluded.

statements.text: Spatial analysis implicated the CD44-LGALS9 axis in endothelial cell remodeling and T-cell suppression around B3 cells.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Spatial observations suggest that B3 cells may contribute to an immunosuppressive microenvironment, with the CD44-LGALS9 axis acting as a possible mediator of endothelial cell remodeling and T-cell suppression.
statements.note: This is the reported spatial finding about B3 cells and that axis.

statements.text: Somatic APC variants fitting SBS88 or ID18 appeared in at least one adenoma or carcinoma in 29% of patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: NGS showed somatic APC variants fitting SBS88 or ID18 in at least one colorectal adenoma or carcinoma in 29% of patients.
statements.note: The 29% figure and the lesion criterion match.

statements.text: Patients with variants fitting the colibactin signatures carried more pks genes in their stool than patients without.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Fecal metagenomic analyses revealed enriched presence of pks genes in patients with somatic variants fitting colibactin-associated signatures compared to patients without variants fitting colibactin-associated signatures.
statements.note: Faecal pks enrichment in that patient group is the reported result.

statements.text: Eradicating pks-positive Escherichia coli reduced adenoma formation in these polyposis patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings further support colibactins ability to mutagenize colorectal mucosa and contribute to the development of colorectal adenomas and carcinomas explaining a relevant part of patients with unexplained polyposis.
statements.note: The study links signatures to bacterial presence; no eradication or intervention outcome is reported.

statements.text: Whole-genome sequencing found SBS88 and ID18 depleted in the patients whose variants fitted these signatures.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: mutational signature analyses showed enrichment of SBS88 and ID18 in patients with variants fitting these signatures in NGS compared to patients without
statements.note: Those signatures were enriched, not depleted, in that group.

statements.text: Somatic alterations fell primarily in XRCC1, ITPKB, ABCB1 and OPRM1, while recurrent variants clustered in TP53, CDKN2A and TERT.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: whereas somatic alterations were primarily detected in established cancer-associated genes such as TP53 , CDKN2A , and TERT
statements.note: The two gene sets are swapped: the somatic alterations hit TP53, CDKN2A and TERT.

statements.text: Ten paired tumor and adjacent normal tissues, twenty samples in all, underwent whole-exome sequencing.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Paired tumor and adjacent normal tissues from ten OSCC samples (total n = 20 samples) were subjected to WES to identify somatic and germline-associated variants.
statements.note: The pairing and both counts match the stated design.

statements.text: Recurrent germline-associated variants formed a broad background, outnumbering the comparatively few tumor-specific somatic mutations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The analysis identified a broad background of recurrent germline-associated variants alongside a comparatively limited number of tumor-specific somatic mutations
statements.note: This balance between germline and somatic variation is the reported finding.

statements.text: Areca nut users in this cohort carried more TP53 mutations than non-users.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains a major public health challenge, particularly in South Asian populations where environmental exposures such as tobacco and areca nut consumption contribute significantly to disease burden.
statements.note: Exposures are named as background; no mutation comparison by exposure status is reported.

statements.text: S. mutans alone drove the biofilm to about pH 4, while V. parvula converted lactate to acetic and propionic acids and lifted it to about pH 5.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: S. mutans produces lactic acid from carbohydrates resulting in a final biofilm pH∼4, while V. parvula metabolizes lactate to acetic and propionic acids resulting in pH∼5.
statements.note: Both pH values and the acids produced match.

statements.text: Transposon insertions at loci unrelated to deacidification also worsened biofilm health.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Transposon insertions in other loci unrelated to deacidification had no impact on biofilm health.
statements.note: Such insertions had no impact on biofilm health.

statements.text: An intact lutABC operon was needed to improve biofilm health, shown by plasmid complementation of a lutB transposon mutant.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: An intact lutABC operon was required to enhance biofilm health, as demonstrated by plasmid-based complementation of a lutB transposon mutant.
statements.note: The requirement and the complementation experiment are both reported.

statements.text: Colonizing children with V. parvula reduced the number of carious lesions they developed.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Interfering with this pathway would interrupt the mutually beneficial relationship between S. mutans and V. parvula that leads to their co-association in caries, root caries, and early childhood caries.
statements.note: Caries is named as the clinical context of co-association; no clinical outcome was measured.

statements.text: hsa-miR-144-3p emerged as the key disulfidptosis-related micro-RNA significantly associated with glioblastoma.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We identified hsa-miR-144-3p as a key disulfidptosis-related miRNA significantly associated with GBM.
statements.note: This identification is the study's central reported result.

statements.text: miR-144-3p expression showed no significant association with immune checkpoint expression or immune cell infiltration patterns.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Moreover, its expression was significantly associated with immune checkpoint expression and immune cell infiltration patterns
statements.note: Both associations were significant.

statements.text: miR-144-3p acts on SLC7A11 to control disulfidptosis in glioblastoma cells.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study reveals that the disulfide-related gene miR-144-3p, as a potential key miRNA may improve the prognosis by regulating immune cell infiltration and promoting the expression of immune checkpoints in GBM and serve as a target in GBM treatment.
statements.note: The proposed role is immune-related; no messenger RNA target of miR-144-3p is identified.

statements.text: miR-144-3p was enriched in immune-related pathways and correlated strongly with stromal score, immune score and tumor purity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Functional analyses revealed that miR-144-3p was markedly enriched in immune-related pathways and strongly correlated with stromal score, immune score, and tumor purity.
statements.note: The enrichment and all three correlations are reported.

statements.text: Nucleosomes gained in tumour tissue were roughly 20-fold enriched at CpG islands, many marking promoters of DNA-binding protein genes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with ∼20-fold enrichment at CpG islands, a large fraction of which marked promoters of genes encoding DNA-binding proteins
statements.note: The enrichment factor and the promoter class match the reported result.

statements.text: Plasma cfDNA nucleosome maps on their own identified which participants had breast cancer.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Here we have generated high resolution nucleosome maps in paired tumour and normal tissues from the same breast cancer patients using MNase-assisted histone H3 ChIP-seq and compared them with the corresponding cfDNA from blood plasma.
statements.note: cfDNA was compared with the tissue maps; no diagnostic classification of patients is reported.

statements.text: Average spacing between nucleosomes was 5-10 bp shorter in tumour tissue than in normal tissue.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: tumour tissues were characterised by a 5-10 bp decrease in the average distance between nucleosomes (nucleosome repeat length, NRL)
statements.note: The reported shift in nucleosome repeat length is a decrease of this size.

statements.text: The shift in nucleosome repeat length in tumours ran opposite to the difference seen between pluripotent and differentiated cells.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: which is qualitatively similar to the differences between pluripotent and differentiated cells
statements.note: The tumour shift was qualitatively similar to that difference, not opposite to it.

statements.text: Tumour mutational burden separated responders from non-responders in bladder cancer but not in lung cancer.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In NSCLC, tumor mutational burden (TMB) did not differ significantly between responders and non-responders, while in MIBC, higher TMB was linked to better responses.
statements.note: TMB discriminated response in bladder cancer only.

statements.text: In lung cancer, responders were enriched for FGFR3 and neural crest differentiation pathways, while non-responders showed active inflammatory and immune pathways.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Pathway analysis showed that NSCLC responders had active inflammatory and immune pathways, while pathways enriched in non-responders related to FGFR3 and neural crest differentiation, associated to resistance mechanisms.
statements.note: The two pathway sets are swapped between responders and non-responders.

statements.text: LINE-1 activation correlated with the number of predicted neoantigens in the bladder tumours.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In MIBC, responders had alterations in DNA repair, leading to more neoantigens and a stronger ICI response.
statements.note: Neoantigen load is tied to DNA repair alterations; nothing links it to LINE-1 activity.

statements.text: LINE-1 activation was positively linked to checkpoint inhibitor response, most clearly in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we found that LINE-1 activation was positively linked to ICI response, especially in MIBC
statements.note: This positive link and its strongest setting are reported.

statements.text: The lesion areas showed only pure atypical carcinoid or pure small cell carcinoma morphology, without hybrid features.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: the lesion areas also present hybrid morphological characteristics of both tumors
statements.note: Hybrid morphology of both tumour types was observed in the lesion areas.

statements.text: The two tumour components shared 160 identical somatic mutations, about 16% of the total in each component.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the two tumor components shared a set of 160 identical somatic mutations (accounting for approximately 16% of the total mutations in each component)
statements.note: Both the shared mutation count and the percentage match.

statements.text: Both components had lost RB1 expression, with Ki67 low and TP53 high in the carcinoid and the reverse in the small cell carcinoma.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: atypical carcinoids exhibited a low Ki67 proliferative index, high TP53 expression, and loss of RB1 expression, whereas small cell lung carcinomas showed a high Ki67 proliferative index, low TP53 expression, and loss of RB1 expression
statements.note: The immunophenotypes match, with RB1 loss shared by both components.

statements.text: The small cell carcinoma component responded to platinum-etoposide chemotherapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study delineates a dynamic evolutionary process within the pulmonary neuroendocrine tumor spectrum, confirming that a subset of atypical carcinoids can progress to small cell lung carcinoma through a transformation pathway.
statements.note: The work establishes a transformation pathway; no treatment response data are reported.

statements.text: In the GALAXY cohort the model labelled 307 patients high risk and 1248 low risk, with a hazard ratio of 2.60.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In GALAXY, the DL-model categorized 307 patients as DL high-risk and 1248 patients as DL low-risk (p<0.001; HR 2.60, CI 95% 2.11-3.21).
statements.note: Both group sizes and the hazard ratio match.

statements.text: Within the MRD-negative group, deep-learning high versus low risk separated disease-free survival with a hazard ratio of 2.37.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the MRD-negative group into DL high-risk (n=226) and DL low-risk (n=1088) (HR 2.37 CI 95% 1.73-3.23; p<0.001)
statements.note: That hazard ratio is reported for the MRD-negative split.

statements.text: The deep-learning score predicted overall survival as well as disease-free survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We developed a DL pipeline utilizing vision transformers to predict disease-free survival (DFS) based on histological hematoxylin & eosin (H&E) stained whole slide images (WSIs) from patients with resectable stage II-IV CRC.
statements.note: The endpoint throughout is disease-free survival; overall survival is never reported.

statements.text: Among MRD-negative patients predicted to be at high deep-learning risk, adjuvant chemotherapy brought no disease-free survival benefit.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: MRD-negative patients had significantly longer DFS when predicted as DL high-risk and treated with ACT (HR 0.48, CI 95% 0.27-0.86; p= 0.01)
statements.note: That group did benefit, with a hazard ratio of 0.48 at p = 0.01.

statements.text: In culture, the TYK2 D810V mutation boosted T cell effector functions and cytokine production.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In vitro, TYK2 D810V enhanced T cells effector functions and cytokine production.
statements.note: Both effects are reported for the mutation in vitro.

statements.text: TYK2 D810V was commoner in tumour infiltrating lymphocytes from patients who responded to checkpoint blockade.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Among these mutations, TYK2 D810V was recurrently observed in patients with diverse cancer types.
statements.note: Recurrence across cancer types is reported, with no link to any therapy response.

statements.text: Mice carrying a germline Tyk2 D807V mutation stayed healthy and free of autoimmune disease yet showed stronger anti-tumour effects.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: These mice were healthy and did not develop autoimmune disorders. However, they possessed enhanced anti-tumor effects in the context of syngeneic and autochthonous cancer models.
statements.note: Health, absence of autoimmunity and enhanced anti-tumour effects are all reported.

statements.text: Adoptive transfer of Tyk2 D807V CD8-positive T cells accelerated cancer growth.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Adoptive therapy with Tyk2 D807V CD8⁺ T cells also decreased cancer growth.
statements.note: That transfer decreased cancer growth.

statements.text: The blaKPC-2 gene sat within transposons such as Tn4401a and Tn3-like elements and within insertion sequences ISKpn27 and ISKpn6.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the bla KPC-2 gene was embedded within transposons (Tn4401a, Tn4401i, and Tn3-like) and insertion sequences (ISKpn27 and ISKpn6)
statements.note: These are exactly the elements the gene was embedded in.

statements.text: Susceptibility testing showed the strains stayed susceptible to polymyxins despite their carbapenem resistance.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing revealed multidrug resistance, including coresistance to carbapenems and polymyxins, among Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterobacter asburiae, and Enterobacter kobei strains.
statements.note: Coresistance to carbapenems and polymyxins was found.

statements.text: Treated effluent leaving these plants still carried carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In this study, we performed genomic characterization of CPE strains recovered from raw wastewater samples from the influents of different WWTPs.
statements.note: Strains came from influent samples only; nothing is reported about treated effluent.

statements.text: blaKPC-2 was detected in Klebsiella pneumoniae high-risk clones ST11 and ST307 and in Enterobacter asburiae ST384.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the bla KPC-2 gene was detected in K. pneumoniae strains belonging to high-risk clones ST11 (capsular types KL64 and KL15) and ST307 (capsular type KL102), and E. asburiae ST384
statements.note: These are the clones and sequence types reported to carry the gene.

statements.text: Trimming of the poly(A) tail follows RNA decay rather than preceding it.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Trimming of poly(A) tail is a rate-limiting step that precedes the RNA decay
statements.note: Poly(A) trimming precedes RNA decay.

statements.text: Loss of CCR4a strongly derepressed transposable elements in Arabidopsis and let them mobilize.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We found that the loss of CCR4a leads to strong derepression and mobilization of TEs in Arabidopsis.
statements.note: Both derepression and mobilization follow CCR4a loss.

statements.text: Loss of CCR4a also lowered DNA methylation at the derepressed transposable elements.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Here, we show that mRNA deadenylation is critical for controlling transposons in Arabidopsis.
statements.note: The mechanism studied is cytoplasmic RNA turnover; no DNA methylation measurement is reported.

statements.text: The transposable elements controlled by CCR4a differ largely from those controlled by RDR6, the enzyme making cytoplasmic siRNAs.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: CCR4a regulates a largely distinct set of TEs from those controlled by RNA-dependent RNA Polymerase 6 (RDR6), a key enzyme that produces cytoplasmic siRNAs
statements.note: The two pathways are reported to act on largely distinct element sets.
